text:
The satin of pages leafed through in books models

a woman so beautiful

that when one is not reading, one looks at that woman sadly

without daring to speak to her, without daring to tell her she is so beautiful

that what one is about to learn is priceless

This woman passes imperceptibly amid a murmur of flowers

Sometimes she turns among the printed seasons

to ask the time, or better still pretends to contemplate some

jewels straight on

as real creatures do not

And the world dies, a rupture occurs in the rings of air

A tear in the place of the heart

The morning papers bring singers whose voices have the color of

sand on tender and dangerous riverbanks

And sometimes the evening papers give way to girls leading

chained animals

But the most beautiful thing lies in the interval between certain letters

where hands whiter than the horn of the stars at noon

plunder a nest of white swallows

so that it may always rain

so low, so low that the wings can no longer mingle

Hands by which one climbs to arms so light

that the vapor of meadows in their graceful spirals above

the ponds is their imperfect mirror

Arms that articulate only with the exceptional danger of a

body made for love

whose belly calls to the sighs shed by the thickets

full of veils

and that have of the earthly only the immense frozen truth of the sleds of

gazes across the whole white expanse

of what I will never see again

because of a marvelous blindfold

which is mine in the game of blindman's buff played with wounds

translation.title: The Writings Fly
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem’s book-and-body metamorphosis and its final blindfold image.
